title: Orca ruleset: a competitive ruleset as data
description: A ruleset file (format 1): the legal stages, the stage steps' timers, the clauses, the set's rules (stocks, time, time-outs, ledge-grab limits, tiebreaks), the queue's and the character order's timers and the character select's no-show timer, for one game. Orca compiles this schema in and checks every ruleset against it on load (Source/Core/Core/Orca/Engine/Schema.h, Ruleset.h); the site checks uploads with the same file (YouGame web/src/lib/orca-ruleset.schema.json, a byte copy). Both validators understand exactly the keywords used here (x-orca-keywords) and refuse a schema that uses any other, so the two can't drift; rules a schema can't state are in x-orca-rules, implemented in both and pinned by Tools/orca/mods/ruleset-vectors.json. String lengths are UTF-8 bytes. Every number is an integer.

id.description: The ruleset's name, as mod.json's "rulesets" lists it.

block.description: The match block's ruleset byte for this ruleset (the room header both machines compare). 1 and 2 are the two builtin rulesets'.

stages.description: The legal stages, in the order the steps' defaults use (starters first by convention). Bit i of a stage mask is stage i.

kind.description: The game's own id for the stage (Brawl and Project+: srStageKind), what the stage flows compare and pick.

role.description: starter: game 1's strikes are on the starters; counterpick: later games only.

steps.description: Stage steps (RankedSteps.h). Game 1 is 1-2-1 strikes on the starters; later games, the winner's step (strike or ban) and the loser's pick. Times are whole seconds, then a grace in frames shown as 0:00.

game1Seconds.description: Game 1's three steps: the first strike, the two strikes, the pick.

later.description: The winner's step in later games.

optional.description: The player may skip it (a ban only).

pickSeconds.description: A later game's pick, and the Meta Knight clause's pick.

casualSeconds.description: Casual games: both players name a stage at once.

dsr.description: Full DSR: the loser never picks a stage they won a game on.

iceClimbers.description: A stage that is never legal when either player plays this character.

metaKnight.description: When exactly one player plays this character, the other picks any legal stage, with no strikes.

set.description: A ranked set (RankedSet.h, RankedPPlus.h), and the stocks and time every locked match plays.

wins.description: Games to win the set (the overlay's dots show a best of 3 at most).

timeOut.description: Who decides a timed-out game: judged (the ledge-grab limit, then stocks, then percent, as the clock ran out) or results (the game's own results screen, e.g. a codeset's overtime).

ledgeGrabLimit.description: judged only: a player over the limit loses a timed-out game, unless both are.

tiebreak.description: A tie (a level time-out, or a sudden death) is replayed as a tiebreak game with these rules. Absent: the same game is replayed with the set's rules.

voidAfterTies.description: This many ties in a row void the set.

queue.description: The queue's character select (Policy/Queue.h): both players lock in with Start, then the match starts; at the timer, a casual room times out and a ranked one goes on with the picks. B held skips.

skipFrames.description: Frames B is held to skip.

characterOrder.description: Ranked games 2 and later (Policy/CharOrder.h): one player picks at a time, each turn this long.

readySeconds.description: Ranked character select: a player still without a fighter this long after the other picked is a no-show.

text.description: Printable UTF-8: no control characters, no invalid or surrogate sequences.

ledgeLimit.description: Ledge grabs allowed (the count stops at 255).

x-orca-rules: A ruleset file is one JSON value of at most x-orca-limits.maxBytes bytes and maxDepth levels, nothing after it but whitespace; duplicate keys are refused.

Schema keywords: only x-orca-keywords. Every object lists its properties and has additionalProperties false; every integer has a minimum and a maximum; every string has a minLength, a maxLength and an x-orca-charset; every array has a maxItems. A $ref is #/$defs/<name>.
maxLength and minLength count UTF-8 bytes (a JSON Schema validator counts code points, so it is never stricter).
x-orca-charset id: [a-z0-9-], not starting with '-' (the pattern beside it says the same for other tools). text: valid UTF-8 with no character below U+0020, no U+007F and no U+0080-U+009F.
x-orca-indexOf <pointer>: the integer is below the length of the array at that JSON pointer in the same document.
At least one stage is a starter.
set.ledgeGrabLimit is present exactly when set.timeOut is judged; its characters are distinct.
later.optional is true only for a ban.
Seconds become frames at 60 per second; a step's frames (seconds x 60 + grace) fit 16 bits, and so do css.readySeconds, queue.readySeconds and characterOrder.pickSeconds x 60.
The text is valid UTF-8 with no byte-order mark, and a \u escape for a character above U+FFFF is a surrogate pair.
Every number is written as an exact integer of magnitude at most 2^53 - 1, in at most 32 bytes (30, 30.0, 3e1 and -0 are integers; 0.5 and 1e-400 are not).
